overview: The Bahamas is a country of around 700 islands and thousands of smaller cays in the Atlantic Ocean, south-east of Florida. Its capital, Nassau, is on the island of New Providence. The Bahamas became independent from the United Kingdom in 1973, and the British monarch is still its head of state. Tourism and banking are the main parts of its economy.

geography.text: The islands are low and flat, built from limestone and coral, and surrounded by shallow, clear turquoise water. They lie in the path of Atlantic hurricanes. Andros is the largest island, and off its coast runs one of the longest barrier reefs in the world.

history.text: The Lucayan people lived on the islands when Columbus made his first landing in the Americas there in 1492; within a few decades they had been wiped out by slavery and disease. The British settled the islands in the 1600s, and Nassau became a base for pirates. The Bahamas became independent in 1973.

events.title: Columbus lands
events.text: Columbus's first landfall in the Americas is in the Bahamas.

events.title: Pirates driven out
events.text: A British governor ends Nassau's days as a pirate base.

government.text: The Bahamas is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor-General. The Prime Minister leads the government and must have the support of the elected House of Assembly.

economy.text: Tourism makes up most of the economy, with millions of visitors arriving by cruise ship and plane each year. Banking and financial services are the second pillar. The Bahamas has no income tax.

culture.text: Junkanoo, a street parade with goatskin drums, cowbells and huge colourful costumes, takes place on Boxing Day and New Year's Day. Conch, a large sea snail, is the national dish. Many Bahamians have roots among enslaved Africans and Loyalists who arrived after the American Revolution.

items.title: Junkanoo
items.text: A late-night street parade on Boxing Day and New Year's Day.

items.title: Blue holes
items.text: Deep underwater caves, including Dean's Blue Hole, over 200 m deep.

sport.text: Athletics brings the Bahamas its greatest successes. Shaunae Miller-Uibo won Olympic gold in the 400 m in 2016 and 2020, and the country has won Olympic relay gold. Basketball and baseball are also popular, and several Bahamians have played in the NBA.

items.text: The 'Golden Girls' won Olympic gold in the women's 4 x 100 m relay.

didYouKnow: The Bahamas is made up of about 700 islands and more than 2,000 rocks and cays.

keyPeople.name: Sidney Poitier
keyPeople.text: Grew up in the Bahamas; the first Black man to win the Oscar for Best Actor.
